name: OSINT — People, Infrastructure & Metadata
tagline: Passive intelligence on people, exposed infrastructure, and document metadata — for authorized recon and for auditing your own digital footprint.

tools.name: Sherlock
tools.desc: Checks a username across 400+ platforms using HTTP status/pattern heuristics and returns every profile that exists; the reference CLI for username enumeration, actively maintained.
tools.when: Confirm which sites a username you own is registered on so you can harden or clean up your own footprint.

tools.name: Maigret
tools.desc: Collects a username dossier across 3000+ sites with account-type tags (social, dating, code) and exports HTML/PDF/JSON reports; picks up a fresh site list on each run.
tools.when: When Sherlock's pass/fail list is not enough and you want an exportable report of everywhere a handle you control appears.

tools.name: Blackbird
tools.desc: Blazing-fast username enumerator that checks 500+ services with thread pools and color-coded existence results; built as a speed-focused companion to Sherlock and Maigret.
tools.when: Bulk-check many candidate usernames over a short window, limited to handles and accounts you are authorized to investigate.

tools.name: WhatsMyName
tools.desc: A community-maintained dataset of 700+ sites with exact fingerprints (URI patterns and success/not-found heuristics); the data engine underlying most username checkers.
tools.when: Audit a checker result or drive your own authorized username sweep against a curated, up-to-date site list.

tools.name: HaveIBeenPwned
tools.desc: Definitive breach and password-exposure checker: search any email or domain across a huge corpus of leaked datasets; free web search plus a documented API, with Pwned Passwords openly downloadable.
tools.when: Check whether addresses or domains you control appeared in known breaches, and enforce password-exposure checks on your own estate.

tools.name: IntelligenceX
tools.desc: Dark-web and public-data search engine indexing leaks, paste sites, forums, and code over a 10-year retention window; free tier with API and Telegram bots.
tools.when: Check if your emails, domains, or phone numbers surface in dark-web and paste archives you are authorized to monitor.

tools.name: LeakCheck
tools.desc: Commercial breach aggregator with billions of entries supporting email, username, phone, and live-keyword search; paid tiers unlock full records.
tools.when: Correlate breach hits across emails and passwords, but only on credentials you hold or are authorized to test.

tools.name: Holehe
tools.desc: Checks which 120+ sites an email is registered on by replaying password-recovery flows without mailing the target, so the address is never alerted.
tools.when: Find which platforms a breached or owned email is tied to, so stale accounts you control can be closed or secured.

tools.name: emailrep.io
tools.desc: Hosted API that scores email reputation, flags breach exposure and disposable providers, and lists the mainstream profiles tied to an address; free tier needs no key.
tools.when: Triage a suspicious inbound sender or audit your own addresses as part of a defensive OSINT review.

tools.name: theHarvester
tools.desc: Passive harvester of emails, employee names, subdomains, and reported API keys for a domain across many open sources; the reference domain reconnaissance CLI.
tools.when: Map every email and subdomain publicly linked to a domain you own before hardening mail and DNS.

tools.name: PhoneInfoga
tools.desc: Phone-number OSINT framework that attributes country, area, carrier, and line type and gathers scattered footprint data via configurable scanners; stable but slowly maintained.
tools.when: Resolve a number you own or are authorized to analyze into provider facts before deeper carrier-level checks.

tools.name: Instaloader
tools.desc: Downloads Instagram profiles, posts, hashtags, highlight stories, and their metadata (captions, likes, comments) without an API key; scriptable and actively maintained.
tools.when: Archive a public profile you own, or collect hashtag and post metadata for evidence preservation.

tools.name: Osintgram
tools.desc: Interactive shell that pulls public Instagram profile info, captions, followers, tag lists, and bio-contact strings using a scratch session or a free Hiker API token (educational-use disclaimer included).
tools.when: Relationship analysis on a public profile you operate — who tags, who comments, what contact strings appear in bios.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/Datalux/Osintgram && pip3 install -r requirements.txt

tools.name: snscrape
tools.desc: Python library/CLI that scrapes public posts and profiles to JSONL from several platforms; X/Twitter and Reddit backends are dead behind logins, but Telegram, Weibo, and some Mastodon instances still work.
tools.when: Programmatic retrieval and archiving of public posts on platforms snscrape still supports, e.g. Telegram channels you monitor.

tools.name: ExifTool
tools.desc: Reads, writes, and edits EXIF/GPS/IPTC/XMP metadata across images, PDFs, and Office files; the metadata workhorse behind most document-forensics pipelines.
tools.when: Forensic-grade tag extraction from local files — geolocation, author, generator, timestamps — before release or after acquisition.

tools.name: FotoForensics
tools.desc: Web tool that runs Error Level Analysis (ELA), panel scans, EXIF review, and JPEG quantization analysis to spot digital tampering in an uploaded image.
tools.when: Check whether an image you own or are authorized to examine was edited, and inspect residual metadata block by block.

tools.name: Metagoofil
tools.desc: Dork-driven harvester that finds indexed documents (.pdf, .docx, .xlsx) for a domain and downloads them for metadata stripping; the maintained opsdisk fork ships on Kali.
tools.when: Collect every publicly indexed document on a domain you own so metadata and hidden information can be scrubbed.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/opsdisk/metagoofil && pip3 install -r requirements.txt

tools.name: FOCA
tools.desc: Windows GUI (C# with SQL Server backend) that fingerprints documents across search engines and extracts users, folders, and software into a browsable metadata project.
tools.when: When you have a Windows workstation and want a point-and-click metadata project view for documents you control.

tools.name: VirusTotal
tools.desc: Industry-standard crowdsourced engine for hashes, samples, URLs, and IP/domain reputation with 90+ AV engines, plus passive DNS and threat-signal context.
tools.when: Check a file hash, URL, or IP you are investigating against years of crowdsourced detections during authorized analysis.

tools.name: ipinfo.io
tools.desc: IP address datasets and API for location, ISP, ASN, company, and privacy-risk signals; free lookup tier covers geolocation and network attribution.
tools.when: Resolve an IP address you are investigating into location, provider, and ASN context.

tools.name: ipapi.co
tools.desc: Free IP geolocation API returning country, city, ISP, timezone, and currency for any address; also offers bulk and commercial JSON/CSV plans.
tools.when: Script location lookups for lists of IPs appearing in your own logs.

tools.name: Google Maps
tools.desc: Global mapping, Street View, and satellite imagery search; the core visual geolocation and place-lookup surface for OSINT.
tools.when: Correlate landmarks, signage, or geotagged imagery against the physical world during authorized investigations.

tools.name: Yandex Maps
tools.desc: Alternative globe with strong coverage of Eastern Europe, Russia, and CIS regions plus street-level panoramas; a useful cross-check for place and imagery comparison.
tools.when: Cross-check locations and side-by-side imagery with Google Maps when coverage hints at CIS or Eurasian regions.

tools.name: Shodan
tools.desc: The reference internet device and service search engine indexing banners, ports, vulnerabilities, and exposure history for any IP or domain; also exposes free InternetDB lookups.
tools.when: See exactly which ports and services your public IP ranges expose right now — and how long that exposure has existed — before closing them.

tools.name: Censys
tools.desc: Internet-wide scan platform over hosts, services, and certificates with structured query language and host/cert/web-property APIs; free tier includes search and lookups.
tools.when: Certificate-centric inventory and pivots — find every host presenting a given cert — or query structured service data beyond free Shodan limits.

tools.name: Netlas
tools.desc: Scanning platform over billions of indexed hosts supporting IPv4/IPv6, full response-body regex, DNS, WHOIS, and certificate search with a REST API; free tier capped near 50 requests/day.
tools.when: Lucene/regex search across full HTTP response bodies when Shodan banners are too shallow for your authorized query.

tools.name: DNSDumpster
tools.desc: One-page passive DNS mapping tool that enumerates subdomains, MX/TXT/SPF records, and hosts onto an interactive network map for a domain.
tools.when: Fast visual pass over the subdomain and mail infrastructure of a domain you own before deeper enumeration.

tools.name: SecurityTrails
tools.desc: Commercial passive DNS and subdomain intelligence with historical DNS records, certificate timelines, and connected-domain data via REST API.
tools.when: Retrieve DNS history and subdomain changes over time for a domain you operate, straight into scripts.

tools.name: crt.sh
tools.desc: Open certificate-transparency log search; returns every issued certificate — and therefore every hostname — for a domain, sorted by issue date.
tools.when: Enumerate all hostnames that ever had a public certificate for domains you own, including retired staging hosts.

tools.name: Hurricane Electric BGP
tools.desc: Global BGP, IPv6, and routing intelligence: AS numbers, prefixes, IXP membership, route announcements, and peer relationships in a browsable web database.
tools.when: Attribute an IP or prefix to its ASN and understand routing relationships for infrastructure you analyze.

tools.name: RIPEstat
tools.desc: RIPE NCC's data API for IP/ASN attribution, route history, geolocation, and abuse contacts; queryable over REST with ready-made widgets.
tools.when: Programmatic WHOIS/ASN and routing lookups for lists of IPs or prefixes you are researching.

tools.name: DomainTools
tools.desc: Commercial WHOIS and domain-intel suite (WhoIs, reverse whois, registration history, DNSHistory, Iris) maintained for 20+ years; priced via API/subscription tiers.
tools.when: Full WHOIS history and reverse-ownership pivots on domains involved in authorized investigations.

tools.name: OpenCorporates
tools.desc: Open database of millions of companies worldwide extracted from public registries; unique API for entities, officers, and filings across many jurisdictions.
tools.when: Discover corporate structure, officers, and cross-jurisdiction registrations behind a company you are authorized to research.

tools.name: Companies House (UK)
tools.desc: UK government registry of companies, officers, people with significant control (PSC), and filings, exposed through a free public API.
tools.when: Company, director, and beneficial-owner lookups for UK-registered entities.

tools.name: SEC EDGAR
tools.desc: US SEC's full-text filings database (10-K, 8-K, S-1, proxies) exposing financials, executives, and subsidiaries; free API with fair-use limits.
tools.when: Pull US-listed company filings for financial and personnel intelligence.

tools.name: Crunchbase
tools.desc: Venture and funding profile database with financing rounds, acquisitions, growth-stage signals, and key-people digests for startups and private companies.
tools.when: Sketch the funding trajectory, investors, and key people of a private company you analyze.

tools.name: GitHub Code Search
tools.desc: GitHub's built-in search over the public code index with operators for language, path, and extension; also surfaces users, commits, and leaked-token suspects.
tools.when: Find public code, configs, and secrets that mention an identifier you own, and review your own repositories' exposure.

tools.name: Sourcegraph
tools.desc: Public-code search engine with regex, literal, and symbol-aware queries across open repositories; good for finding leaked patterns and re-used infrastructure.
tools.when: Regex-wide sweep of public code for a credential prefix, domain, or package name you are attributing.

tools.name: GitDorker
tools.desc: Automates GitHub 'dork' queries from a 3000+-entry dork list through the search APIs to surface exposed files, keys, and configs in public repositories.
tools.when: Glob for suspicious files and secrets across public repos related to your own organization or authorized targets.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/obheda12/GitDorker && pip3 install -r requirements.txt

tools.name: Nosey Parker
tools.desc: Fast secret-scanner that extracts API tokens and credentials from git histories with high-precision regex and entropy rules; written in Rust for large corpora.
tools.when: Scan cloned public repositories (e.g., ones you own) for historic secrets before they are abused.

tools.name: Blockchain.com Explorer
tools.desc: Bitcoin block explorer with address, transaction, and pending-mempool views plus webhooks and an authenticated explorer API.
tools.when: Trace bitcoin addresses and transaction flows connected to a case you are authorized to investigate.

tools.name: Etherscan
tools.desc: Reference Ethereum block explorer with address, token, contract-code, and event-log analysis and a free API; covers other EVM chains via sibling explorers.
tools.when: Analyze EVM addresses, token transfers, and smart-contract interactions you are investigating.

tools.name: WalletExplorer
tools.desc: Clusters bitcoin addresses into services where possible, letting you see a wallet's whole activity — including market aggregation endpoints.
tools.when: View a bitcoin address in service context and reveal associated addresses during authorized tracing work.

tools.name: BitcoinAbuse
tools.desc: Public API and searchable database of bitcoin addresses reported for scams and fraud, with user-submitted evidence and descriptions.
tools.when: Check whether an address you are investigating carries attached abuse reports.

tools.name: Wayback Machine
tools.desc: The Internet Archive's store of hundreds of billions of web snapshots; view any URL as it existed historically, with CDX listings and full-text site search.
tools.when: Recover removed pages, track historical site changes, and capture evidence before content disappears.

tools.name: waybackpy
tools.desc: Python client for the Wayback and CDX APIs: save snapshots, query availability, and stream archive listings programmatically.
tools.when: Scripted archival and CDX queries to build change-history timelines for URLs you monitor.

tools.name: Archive.today
tools.desc: Independent web snapshot service that mirrors pages on demand and blocks most crawlers; a useful second capture layer parallel to the Wayback Machine.
tools.when: Save a live page as evidence through an independent archive when you want redundancy across capture providers.

tools.name: Common Crawl
tools.desc: Petabyte-scale open crawl corpus refreshed monthly (WARC/WAT/WET files) with a URL index API; reconstruct what a site published even without per-page snapshots.
tools.when: Pull historical page versions or URL-level index data for content you have permission to analyze.

tools.name: Ahmia
tools.desc: Ethical search engine for the Tor network with support for .onion and I2P; continuously indexes dark-web pages and filters illegal content.
tools.when: Index and discover .onion pages relevant to a monitoring program you are authorized to run.

tools.name: Dark.fail
tools.desc: Trusted, hand-verified directory of live .onion marketplaces and services with uptime status; a safe entry index rather than an in-depth search engine.
tools.when: Locate legitimate .onion services and verify their current uptime during authorized dark-web research.

tools.name: DeHashed
tools.desc: Commercial breach database covering email, username, phone, IP, and password hashes with fuzzy search and cross-referencing across billions of records; subscription required for full records.
tools.when: Correlate leaked credentials and keys across datasets — only for accounts you own or are contracted to test.

tools.name: Pastebin Search
tools.desc: Pastebin's own search across public pastes, combinable with search engines via site: dorks; useful for monitoring dropped credentials and dumps.
tools.when: Monitor public paste dumps that mention an organization or domain you are authorized to defend.

tools.name: SpiderFoot
tools.desc: Automated OSINT correlation engine with 200+ modules and a YAML correlation engine, surfaced through a web UI, CLI, and API; built to map an attack surface and connect entities.
tools.when: A broad sweep of a domain, IP, or email you own to correlate entities across many free data sources in a single scan.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/smicallef/spiderfoot && pip3 install -r requirements.txt

tools.name: Maltego
tools.desc: Commercial graph-based link-analysis platform (desktop and browser) whose transforms reach identity, breach, and infrastructure datasets; free Community Edition exists with result limits.
tools.when: Investigative link analysis where a visual graph of who connects to whom beats raw JSON output.

tools.name: Google Hacking Database (GHDB)
tools.desc: Canonical reference catalog of search-engine operators and example queries that surface exposed files, login panels, and misconfigurations in public indexes.
tools.when: Compose and reuse proven dorks to audit what public indexes expose about domains you own.
